blocks.text: The bar: a portal is a set piece: glass cut to the doorway's own opening, an arch of this world's own stone around it, torches, runes, the far place already visible inside it and its light on this ground; you step out of the far gate facing forward onto a composed view, the gate at your back.

// spawn: { id: "gate-east", tags: ["portal"], behavior: "scripts/gate.js", state: { link: "+cellar#gate-west" }, rotation: 90, primitive: { kind: "arch", width: 2.6, height: 3.4, depth: 0.3 }, // physics: { body: "static", trigger: true }, material: { kind: "scripted", script: "engine/portal-ember", view: { link: "+cellar#gate-west", spill: 2, sound: 1 } }, // children: [ { id: "arch", primitive: { kind: "archway", width: 3.4, height: 3.8, depth: 0.6, thickness: 0.4 }, physics: "static", material: { color: "#6b6258", roughness: 0.95 } } ] } // spawn, in the cellar, the twin: the same with id "gate-west", rotation: 270, both links "+main#gate-east" export function onTriggerEnter(ctx, other) { ctx.cross(other, ctx.self.state.link); } export function onCross(ctx, other) { ctx.emit("playSound", { clip: "cdn/gate-chime.mp3", position: ctx.self.worldFeetPosition }); } export function onRefuse(ctx, other, verdict) { ctx.emit("uiEvent", { name: "refused", payload: { message: verdict.message } }); // ui.js draws what happened }

The glass is the opening's shape: an arch of the opening's width and height fills an archway of that profile edge to edge (frame width + 2 × thickness by height + thickness); any other doorway takes a scripted-geometry glass cut to it (→geometry). material.view paints any shape.

spawn browse --creator <handle> (or spawn browse "<words>") finds another creator's world, published or not, no pasted link; its address is the link, link: "@ress/cathedral +main" (the card at --address names its places). gate.destination.onlineCount counts who plays there (null until known).

#exit is the gate you step out of, written on BOTH gates. Gates come in pairs, sized alike, each facing its approach side, the way you walk out (a gate faces −Z at rotation: 0). A link naming only the place (+cellar) steps out of the far gate whose link names yours back; with no such gate you land at the place's arrival, else its spawn: a cut, not a doorway. The gate's script crosses the body (onTriggerEnter), waiting for the glass, keeping your heading; a body crossing itself lands at once at the exit, facing out. A seated rider has no body: the car meets the glass and crossing it takes the driver, so a players-only gate moves neither.

A door's link is where it leads, for everyone (its glass, warm-up and crossing); it wears that glass, tinted by color; material.view: null leaves a plain face that still crosses. A linkless door sending each walker somewhere of theirs (player.den, player.saved) holds them at the glass while it loads; instead each player's script spawns theirs with audience: "local" and that link.

The glass: material.view: { link, spill, sound, oneWay }: the far place seen through the face, its light on your ground. oneWay: true: one face, veiled and closed behind. Presets script: "engine/portal-<name>": glass, water, ember, ink, veil, mirror-break, pixel, stained-glass, static, starfield, aurora, honeycomb, oil-slick (the rift is the return door's torn disc, not a slab): a preset styles the frame; the far world inside stays clear and still at every distance (params: { warp: 1 } restores the old whole-glass look); a door with no preset samples the far world with ctx.view(offset) (its ctx: spawn api builtin/three).

material.view: { camera } is a camera; spawn api ViewCamera has the rest. camera: "mirror" is a mirror (hideLocalPlayer hides your body from the screen's eye alone): a plane in material: { color: "#0b0e12", view: { camera: "mirror" } }; camera: { eye, aim, fov } is a placed camera: a security monitor, or a map (eye high, aiming down, projection: "orthographic", orthoSize). layers picks what a camera draws (default ["default"]): icons on ["icons"] show on a map with layers: ["default", "icons"], roofs on ["roofs"] where the screen's camera.layers names them, a ghost on ["ghost"] in { mirror: true, layers: ["default", "ghost"] }. camera: { parent: id, eye, aim, fov } rides that thing in its frame: move or turn it, never re-pose each tick. ctx.view.camera takes both, never place. place: "<id>" films that place of this world while a player near the face sees it. A view draws only while a player sees its face, smaller and rarer on a weak device.
camera: { parent: id, eye, aim, fov }

The frame is most of the door: an arch, a lintel, braziers, a worn threshold, the far side's spill lighting it; the refusal spoken by the door. An arrival is latched until it steps clear, then turning around walks straight back. Arriving from ANOTHER world whose far gate does not link back opens a return rift behind the traveler for 30 s, shaped by returnDoor on the arrival place: { lifetime } its seconds, false none; a door WITHIN your world opens none: build its way back.

Your held and worn things come through a door WITHIN your world. Into ANOTHER world, even one you edit, its admits() decides, at page loads too: the arrival place's policy.admits, else the world root's, else only its world.config.yaml visitorsCarry: true (default off). What you ride crosses on those terms or bounces whole at the glass. Write that world's admits() with the door (new game: in its brief; not yours: tell the creator). admits() reads how a thing comes in ctx.crossing.actor.attachment: "attached" (held or worn), "ridden" or "loose". A refused thing is never lost: it waits in player.pocket (ctx.self.pocket, read-only [{ objectId, kind, reason, from }], [] when empty), and returns to the hand in the next world admitting it (by default home admits its own, your den yours). With no body there, your carry script's drop with an empty hand and a full pocket answers the pocket (a notice your HUD draws from reason).
Abroad the host's scripts turn your body and what it holds (a fresh world: toward the walk), so a held thing aiming with the eye aims from the look.

Your player.state rides the door too. At arrival that world's save of you wins for every key it holds; a carried key it lacks stands on you there, over the template default, and enters its save only when a script there writes it.

A travelling behavior runs abroad under the host's ceiling (its world.config.yaml foreign: { faculties: [...] }; unset = every word); one declaring nothing gets all but write:world. A top-level export const faculties = ["write:self"] narrows it to the words it names, of render, animate, audio, physics, collide, follow, attach, script, emit, spawn, write:self, write:world, voxel; reads, timers, on and queries are always free. A declared word the ceiling lacks pockets that behavior (the runtime log's crossing.behavior.pocketed); the thing keeps its others and re-binds it at home.

ctx.self.objectId, world:<birth>#<name>, names a thing in every world; id is bare at home, the address abroad. A player and what spawns under one keep its session id player/… as both; ctx.world.id tells where. Key a ledger row on objectId (a player's on userId); query({ objectId }) finds a thing after a hop.
